excitation_report: With sigma=0.2 A/s on dI_dt and t in [0, 0.5]s, the new eddy-current term (eddy_coeff*(M_sat*tanh(I/I_ref)-M)/tau_M inside the RHS, coupled through the L_sat_coeff*I^2 correction) drives the child trajectory 1.734 A/s (8.67*sigma) away from the parent trajectory, peaking at t~0.08s while M lags the fast I rise. All other terms (V_source drive, R*I, R_temp_coeff*I^3, V_back_emf_coeff*tanh, k_hyst*M, L_sat_coeff*I^2 correction) dominate portions of the rise from 0 up to steady state (~4-5 A) so each is far above sigma.

t: V->V (confirmed, sole independent time axis)
I: S->S (confirmed, primary dynamic state with IC=0)

M_sat: P->P (confirmed, fixed at 2 to make the eddy driver visible)
eddy_coeff: P->P (confirmed, fixed at 2 V*s per unit magnetization rate, top of the suggested 0-2 range, to lift the new term above 5*sigma)
rationale: Standard series RL step response with strongly nonlinear core: L/R = 0.05s and tau_M = 0.1s, so integrating to t=0.5s covers ~10 electrical time constants and ~5 magnetization time constants — the current rises from 0 to its (nonlinear) steady state, and M chases tanh(I/I_ref) with a visible lag that drives the new eddy term. V_source=12V, R=2 ohm give an ideal steady state ~6A that the nonlinearities pull down to ~4-5A, well inside |I|<I_ref regime where tanh has meaningful curvature. eddy_coeff and M_sat were tuned to keep the new term above 5*sigma at sigma=0.2 A/s while keeping all coefficients within physically reasonable magnitudes for an inductor with a soft magnetic core.
